The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Syed Asif Ali, in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:

sentences.text: traveling in a goods tempo bearing registration No.AP-02-V-9968, the driver of the goods tempo was taking U turn on the highway of Hunegallu, slowly and cautiously by exhibiting proper indications and signals and also by assuring that, no other vehicles were near to his vehicle.

At that time, driver of the Tipper lorry bearing registration No.KA-43-A-3459 came from same direction i.e., from Bengaluru side with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, as a result, driver of the vehicle lost control over his vehicle and the said Tipper lorry went to its wrong side of the road and dashed violently against the said goods tempo.

Due to impact, the deceased was thrown out of the goods tempo and fell on the ground and subsequently the said goods tempo turtled on him and the deceased sustained grievous crush injuries and succumbed to the said injuries on the spot.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/-towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
aged about 49 years, doing vegetable business and earning Rs.50,000/- per month and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners become dark, miserable and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-43-A-3459.
In this regard, Chickballapura Rural Police have registered the case against the driver of the said vehicle in Crime No.102/2023.

As such, the respondent No.1 &
2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to the notice, respondents have appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.
6. The respondent No.1 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has stated that his vehicle bearing registration No.KA-43-A-3459 was insured with the respondent No.2 and had valid policy as on the date of accident from 30.11.2023 to 29.11.2024.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence and it was valid from 19.10.2026 to 24.4.2035.

Further denied about the age,
avocation and income of the deceased.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-43-A-3459 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident, therefore the jurisdictional police have filed a charge sheet against to the respondent No.1 for the offences punishable under section 279, 338,
304A of IPC r/w 3, 181 and 180 of MV Act.

The respondent No.1 has violated the terms and Syeda Reshma Jainab vs Ultimatix Drone Technologies on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109195817/
3 conditions of the policy.

8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners proves that Shri Syed Asif Ali had died in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 23.06.2023 at about 12.30 a.m. near Hunegallu village, on Bengaluru-Hyderabad NH 44, Chickballapura Taluk and district due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing registration No.KA-43-A-3459 in an actionable negligence?
2. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what rate and from whom?
3 . What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
10. On the other hand, respondents have not led any rebuttal evidence on their behalf.

11. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
12.

My findings to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.KA-43-A-3459, alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Syed Asif Ali had died.
As such, the petitioners being the legal heirs of the deceased have filed the claim petition for consideration.

14. On the other hand, the respondents though not disputed the accident and the death of Syed Asif Ali, but strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-43-A-3459.

16. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Syed Reshma Jainab examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon the police documents at Ex.
P1 to Ex
On going through the documents, Ex.
P1- true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.102/2023 of Chickballapura Station.

Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement given by Syed Imthiyaz,
Ex

.P5-true copy of IMV report,
Ex.P6- true copy inquest report, Ex.P7-true copy of P.M.report and Ex.P8-true copy of charge sheet.

18. On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Syed Imthiyaz, the S.H.O. of Chickballapur P.S. have registered the case against the driver of Lorry for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against driver of the Lorry alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC and Section 3, 181, 180 of IMV Act.
19.

On the other hand, though the respondents have taken contention that the accident was not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry, but not made an effort to examine either the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the independent eye witness to prove its contention.

20. PW1 was subjected for cross-examination, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
21. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-43-A-3459 and in the said accident, Syed Asif Ali succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No. 2:
22.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P9 to Ex.P15 i.e., Aadhar cards of the deceased Syeda Reshma Jainab vs Ultimatix Drone Technologies on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109195817/
5 and the petitioner No.1 to 6

The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

23. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife has lost her husband and the petitioner No.2 to 5 are children of the deceased and petitioner No.6 is mother of the deceased have lost their love and affection of the deceased, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
24. The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card, which is marked at Ex.P9 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 12.4.1974.
The accident occurred on 23.6.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 49 years.

For his age, multiplier '13' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
25.
In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing vegetable business and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.

Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased,
it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2023.
By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.
26. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "

sentences.text: Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
28. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are six persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
29. In the present case, deceased was aged about 49 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "13" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of 40-50 years, 25% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,92,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 25% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,92,000+48,000) = Rs.2,40,000/-.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,80,000/-
(Rs.2,40,000-Rs.60,000).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "13" which comes to Rs.23,40,000/-.
30.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

31. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 6 under the head loss of consortium.

LIABILITY:
34.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA-43-A-3459, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore,
the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
35. The respondent No.2 has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Thereby violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
As such, insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

36. In this regard, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer, relevant provision has been inserted stating that, at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license.

37. At the time of arguments the counsel for the respondent No.1 has argued that, driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident, but the police have wrongly registered the case for the offence punishable u/s 3 R/W 181 & 180 of IMV Act and charge sheet was filed for the same offence.
On perusal of the notarised copy of the driving licence, it is clear that, the driver had licence for transport vehicle till 19.10.2026 and for non-transport vehicle till 24.4.2035.
The accident occurred on 23.6.2023.
To disprove the said fact the respondent No.2 has not examined any witness on its behalf.
Hence, it is to be considered that as on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence.
38. As per records insurance policy was valid from 30.11.2022 to 29.11.2023.
The accident had occurred on 23.6.2023.

Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the Syeda Reshma Jainab vs Ultimatix Drone Technologies on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109195817/

Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
39.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,37,000/- (Rupees twenty six lakhs thirty seven thousand only) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 50% and the petitioner No.2 to 6 are entitled the share of 10% each.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 to 3, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of their share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.4 & 5, entire amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice till they attain age of majority.
After attaining the age of majority, entire amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
The guardian of the petitioners is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.6, since the award amount is meagre, entire amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.

28. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are six persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.

the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
